title: SQL-to-CSV drops meeting_instructors links

evidence.quote: Parser only accepts INSERT ... VALUES statements.
SELECT-containing lines are skipped, with meeting_instructors called out in the comment.
Historical sync intentionally emits meeting_instructors INSERT ... SELECT link statements.

reasoning: The historical SQL generator uses INSERT OR IGNORE INTO meeting_instructors ... SELECT to create the meeting/instructor join rows. The CSV converter skips every line containing SELECT and its parser only accepts VALUES inserts, so a CSV-based import will omit meeting_instructors entirely. That corrupts imported historical data by losing the normalized instructor-to-meeting links.
reproduction: Feed sql-to-csv.ts an input containing the meeting_instructors INSERT ... SELECT shape from historical-sync.test.ts; the line is counted as skipped and no meeting_instructors.csv row is produced.
recommendation: Do not blanket-skip SELECT-based inserts. Either preserve them into a post-import SQL artifact that is required to run after CSV import, or add explicit conversion logic for meeting_instructors after meetings and instructors have been imported.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The historical-sync tests prove the SELECT form is generated, but there is no sql-to-csv test that converts that generated SQL or asserts meeting_instructors output exists.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a sql-to-csv regression with a VALUES insert and a meeting_instructors INSERT ... SELECT insert, then assert the converter either produces the join data or emits a required post-import SQL file instead of silently skipping it.
minimumFixScope: scripts/sql-to-csv.ts plus a focused converter test for SELECT-based meeting_instructors statements.
